name: PrismaticConstraint
simple: PrismaticConstraint lets two parts slide along one straight line but never twist. The attachments' X arrows form the sliding track. You can let it slide freely, power it like a motor, or make it slide to an exact spot like a servo. Most of its settings come from SlidingBallConstraint.
analogy: PrismaticConstraint is like a drawer in a desk or a sliding door: it only moves in and out along one track.
whenToUse: Pistons and crushers in an obby
where: Make it with Instance.new("PrismaticConstraint"), set Attachment0 and Attachment1 (one in each part) and put it in workspace. The sliding line is along the attachments' X arrows. Its settings (ActuatorType, TargetPosition, LimitsEnabled...) come from SlidingBallConstraint.

terms.constraint: An invisible rule or connector that the physics engine follows, like 'these two parts must stay stuck together' or 'push this part upward'.
terms.attachment: A tiny invisible point you put inside a part. It has a position AND a direction (its own X, Y and Z arrows). Constraints grab parts by their attachments.
terms.Attachment0 / Attachment1: The two attachments a constraint connects. Attachment0 is usually the one that gets pushed or moved; Attachment1 is the other end or the goal.
terms.axis: An imaginary line something turns around or slides along. An attachment's X axis is its main arrow.
terms.anchored: An anchored part is frozen in place. Physics and constraint forces cannot move it. Set `part.Anchored = false` if you want a constraint to move it.
terms.unanchored: A part that physics is allowed to move. Constraints that push or pull only work on unanchored parts.
terms.force: A push or pull. In Roblox it is measured in Roblox force units (mass x studs per second per second). A bigger number is a harder push.
terms.actuator: The part of a constraint that powers movement by itself, like a motor. ActuatorType picks None (no power), Motor (keep spinning/moving at a speed) or Servo (move to a target spot and stop).
terms.motor (ActuatorType): Keeps turning or sliding at a set speed, like a fan or a car wheel.
terms.servo (ActuatorType): Moves to a set target angle or position and holds there, like a robot arm or an automatic door.
terms.limits: Stops that keep a joint from moving too far, like a door that can only swing 90 degrees.
terms.restitution: Bounciness, from 0 (no bounce, just stops) to 1 (bounces back as hard as it hit).
terms.stud: Roblox's unit of length. A default baseplate grid square is 1 stud; a classic character is about 5 studs tall.
terms.SlidingBallConstraint: The parent class that PrismaticConstraint gets all its sliding settings from, like Velocity, TargetPosition and LowerLimit.
terms.collinear: Lying on the same straight line. The sliding track is the line along the attachments' X arrows.

examples.title: A simple elevator
examples.code:
local shaft = workspace:WaitForChild("Shaft")       -- anchored
local platform = workspace:WaitForChild("Platform") -- unanchored

-- Point both attachments' X arrows straight up (the sliding track)
local upward = CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))
local a0 = Instance.new("Attachment")
a0.Parent = shaft
a0.WorldCFrame = CFrame.new(platform.Position) * upward
local a1 = Instance.new("Attachment")
a1.Parent = platform
a1.WorldCFrame = a0.WorldCFrame

local slider = Instance.new("PrismaticConstraint")
slider.Attachment0 = a0
slider.Attachment1 = a1
slider.ActuatorType = Enum.ActuatorType.Servo
slider.ServoMaxForce = 100000 -- strong enough to lift players
slider.Speed = 8              -- studs per second
slider.TargetPosition = 0     -- start at the bottom
slider.Parent = shaft

while true do
	task.wait(4)
	slider.TargetPosition = 20 -- go up 20 studs
	task.wait(4)
	slider.TargetPosition = 0  -- come back down
end
explain: Rotating the attachments 90 degrees around Z makes their X arrows point up, so the track is vertical.
Servo mode slides to TargetPosition (a distance in studs along the track) and holds there.
Speed controls how fast it slides; ServoMaxForce must beat the weight of the platform plus riders.
The loop sends it up 20 studs and back down every 4 seconds.

gotchas: The track runs along the attachments' X arrows. If it slides sideways, rotate the attachments.
Lifting needs enough force to beat gravity: at least mass x 196.2 for the platform and everything on it.
The sliding settings live on SlidingBallConstraint; look there for full details on each one.
